title: The stupa in the sky (Kern ch. 11)
hookLine: a jeweled stupa rises from the earth; an ancient Buddha inside invites the Buddha to share his seat

cards: The ground opens in the middle of the sermon. Up out of the earth rises a stupa, a tower built to hold the remains of a holy one, and this one is made of jewels.

It climbs, and hangs in the sky, hung with banners and bells, giving off fragrance. Then a voice comes out of it, praising the Buddha for teaching the Lotus. The whole assembly stares up at a reliquary that speaks.
Chapter eleven has begun, and it only gets stranger.

teach.b: First, the tower. A bodhisattva named Mahapratibhana asks: what is this?

teach.h: A BUDDHA WHO CAME TO LISTEN.
teach.b: Inside, the Buddha explains, is the whole body of a Buddha named Prabhutaratna, Many Jewels, from a world long past, who entered final nirvana ages ago. Second, why he came.
While still on the path, Many Jewels vowed: wherever this sutra is taught, in any world, my stupa will rise out of the ground to hear it, and to say, well done.
So a Buddha of the far past has come as a listener, and as a witness. Third, the door.

The assembly wants to see him, but the stupa won't open until the Buddha calls home every form of himself teaching across the worlds in every direction. They arrive, and the worlds are made clean to hold them.

Then the Buddha rises into the air and opens the door with a finger, and the text says it sounds like a great bolt sliding back on a city gate. Inside, Many Jewels sits whole, as if deep in meditation. Fourth, the seat.
Many Jewels moves over and offers half his seat, and the Buddha sits down beside him. Two Buddhas, one from ages ago and one from now, side by side in a jeweled tower in the sky.
Then the Buddha lifts the whole assembly into the air to be near them.
Some readers hear in the seat a picture of the teaching itself: not owned by one age, shared across them. The sutra simply shows it. One seat, two Buddhas, room enough.

how: In Mahayana communities that read the Lotus Sutra, the scene of Many Jewels and Shakyamuni seated together in the stupa is recited and pictured in temple art, and the two Buddhas side by side are honored together.

games.q: what does “the stupa in the sky” mean?
o: a tower of jewels where two Buddhas share one seat
a heavenly palace where gods hear the sutra
a shrine built on a mountaintop for pilgrims

games.q: two on one seat: tap the pairs.
p: Many Jewels, a Buddha of a past age
my stupa will rise wherever this is taught
opened with a finger, like a city gate

s: the stupa stays on the ground
it rises out of the earth and hangs in the sky, jeweled and hung with banners.
Many Jewels came because of a vow he made long ago
he vowed his stupa would rise to hear the sutra wherever it's taught.
the stupa opens as soon as the crowd asks
first the Buddha has to call home every form of himself teaching across the worlds.

games.q: you're Many Jewels, seated in your stupa. the door opens, and the Buddha who taught the sutra stands there. what do you do?
o: stay seated and receive his bow.
move over and offer him half your seat.
step out and give him the whole seat.
games.why: Many Jewels offers half his seat, and the Buddha sits down beside him: two Buddhas, past and present, side by side.

practice: Feel the seat holding you up, and notice how much room you take.

Bring to mind one person you'd usually rank above or below you, a boss, a new hire, an older relative, a kid, and in your mind move over and let them sit beside you, shoulder to shoulder, nobody higher.
Stay there together for a few breaths, then rest with the breath and the seat.

wordCard.voice: The stupa in the sky. A jeweled tower rises from the earth, and the Buddha of a past age inside offers the Buddha half his seat. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: a mound or tower that holds relics; here, one of jewels, rising from the earth.

carryVoice: Your line: two on one seat. The ancient Buddha was the one who moved over first. Until tomorrow.
